content:
Hi everyone,

together with @Gabriele Battimelli we just finished Physlib Search. Everything is open source. Here is the repo: https://github.com/Kernel-Science/physlibsearch.git

It's both the UI and the API – Check out the repo for details.

Technical two sentences – We translate each formal Lean 4 declaration into a natural-language name and description using Gemini guided by dependency-ordered context, then embed both the formal and informal representations into a shared vector space using Gemini Embeddings. At query time, a user's plain-English query (optionally expanded via HyDE into a hypothetical Lean declaration) is embedded and matched against the indexed declarations using approximate nearest-neighbor cosine similarity search in ChromaDB.

We intend to maintain this for the community and keep it free and open source. Feedbacks welcome!!
This is awesome. Do we have something like this for Mathlib? I know we have loogle, but an AI-driven natural-language embedding approach would be really useful for quickly finding specific lemmas.
We were inspired by leansearch! Happy to do it on Mathlib as well, if people need it

Jack McCarthy said:

Do we have something like this for Mathlib?

As well as https://leansearch.net/ there is https://www.leanexplore.com/ and https://leandex.projectnumina.ai/ .
Well I owed you one for the manifold stuff ;-)

An update on Physlib search: with @Gabriele Battimelli we packaged Physlib search as a Claude Skill that can be deployed in whatever IDE. Here is the repo: https://github.com/Kernel-Science/physlibsearch-skill

We worked also on physlibsearch:

  • We fixed the latex issue that @ZhiKai Pong found
  • We updated the Browse section to make it more friendly to navigate
  • We added rule-based filters to the Browse section (theorem, definition, etc)

We'd love to know if these are actually useful for people!
